content: An evaluation of government vehicle fleet maintenance practices highlights challenges such as budget constraints, regulatory compliance, and the adoption of sustainable and cost-optimized approaches. As environmental regulations become more stringent and consumer awareness regarding climate change increases, providers that adopt eco-friendly refrigerant recovery practices and energy-efficient operational models are likely to strengthen their market positioning. The extent to which advanced predictive maintenance and electrification trends are currently implemented in South African operational models is not explicitly clear, as many insights prioritize global contexts without delving into the localized infrastructural and regulatory specifics of the region [1, 4]. Investigations into the historical geographic coverage of auto services in South Africa during the period from 2020 to 2024 indicate a lack of directly relevant historical data, with contemporary sources predominantly emphasizing post-2024 developments, recent regulatory changes, and forward-looking projections [1, 2]. When selecting fleet providers and service partners, mining operators are prioritizing entities that can seamlessly align with their dual mandate of operational resilience and regulatory compliance. Much of the available industry data and regulatory discourse tends to be forward-looking, focusing on future trends, infrastructure progress, and upcoming regulatory amendments affecting public service vehicles, rather than providing retrospective insights into the specific challenges of previous years [41] . For example, discussions surrounding future transport conferences or impending statutory instruments often overshadow the historical data necessary to map the evolution of fleet service requirements comprehensively. Furthermore, official channels often prioritize general mandates and future goals over detailed historical performance metrics [41] . Despite this historical information gap, the current landscape in 2026 clearly dictates that service providers must align themselves with the contemporary and future needs of the logistics sector. The fast-evolving nature of interrelated industries, such as automotive manufacturing and freight forwarding, necessitates that specialized service entities remain agile and continuously update their technical capabilities to meet the stringent demands of modern transport fleets [42] .
